summary:
EarthScope is an environmental data exploration platform that transforms NASA Earth science observations into accessible, understandable, and actionable insights.

Environmental datasets often require specialized tools and statistical knowledge to interpret. EarthScope addresses this challenge through an interactive dashboard where users can explore historical trends, seasonal patterns, unusual environmental observations, and relationships between different indicators.

The platform also provides AI-assisted explanations of scientifically calculated results and experimental forecasts supported by historical performance evaluations. Users can investigate precipitation, temperature, and soil moisture across selected locations in the Philippines without performing complex statistical analysis themselves.

By making NASA environmental information easier to explore and understand, EarthScope aims to support environmental awareness, education, research, and more informed discussions about changing environmental conditions.
details:
The Problem

NASA provides extensive Earth observation datasets, but transforming these measurements into understandable information can be difficult for students, researchers, and the general public. Users often need technical knowledge to process datasets, identify meaningful patterns, and interpret statistical results.

Our Solution

EarthScope simplifies environmental data exploration through an interactive dashboard powered by NASA Earth science observations.

Users can select a study region and environmental indicator to investigate historical changes, seasonal patterns, and unusual observations.

The platform provides:

  • Historical trend analysis: Visualizes long-term changes and evaluates statistical trends.
  • Seasonal exploration: Identifies recurring monthly environmental patterns.
  • Anomaly detection: Highlights observations that differ from historical monthly averages.
  • Variable comparison: Examines relationships between environmental indicators using correlation analysis.
  • AI-assisted interpretation: Explains computed scientific findings in accessible language.
  • Experimental forecasting: Generates short-term environmental forecasts and evaluates their performance against historical observations.

How It Works

NASA environmental datasets are processed and organized into time-series observations. A statistical analysis engine calculates trends, correlations, seasonal averages, and anomalies.

An AI-assisted interpretation system explains these verified results without independently generating numerical statistics. A separate forecasting system estimates future values and compares its predictions against historical observations.

The results are presented through an interactive, responsive web dashboard.

Technology and Resources

The application uses Python, FastAPI, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Plotly. It incorporates Qwen for natural-language interpretation and TimesFM for experimental time-series forecasting.

NASA data sources include GPM IMERG precipitation observations and MERRA-2 environmental datasets accessed through NASA Giovanni and other NASA data services.

Creativity and Innovation

EarthScope combines multiple environmental analysis capabilities within a single accessible interface. Instead of presenting raw satellite and modeled observations alone, it connects statistical analysis, visual exploration, natural-language interpretation, and forecasting.

A key design principle is separating scientific computation from AI-generated explanations. Numerical results are calculated using established statistical methods, while AI helps users understand their meaning and limitations.

Intended Impact

EarthScope is designed for students, educators, researchers, and environmentally curious individuals.

Its goal is to reduce technical barriers to exploring NASA Earth science data, encourage evidence-based environmental discussions, and make environmental research more approachable.

Limitations and Future Development

The current implementation focuses on selected Philippine study areas and environmental indicators. Some datasets represent coarse spatial estimates rather than precise administrative boundaries.

Forecasts are experimental and should not be interpreted as disaster warnings or operational hazard predictions. Future improvements could include broader geographic coverage, additional NASA datasets, and expanded scientific validation.
